week_thesis: Semiconductor sector pullback (profit-taking after record first half) creates a clean rotation opportunity as AI fundamentals remain intact. MU was likely stopped out at -5% from its late-June entry (~$1,133→$975 by July 2, a -14% drawdown), freeing one slot. AMD replaces MU as the primary AI compute play — it has dramatically superior momentum (RS60=+66% vs SPY +44%), a record $5.8B Data Center quarter (+57% YoY), locked OpenAI and Meta 6GW GPU deployment partnerships, and its Helios GPU ramp begins Q3-Q4. Earnings safely on Aug 4 — four weeks away. AMAT holds through the semiconductor equipment correction: the original entry stop ($391) is $212 below the current price ($603); the AI equipment supercycle is confirmed (30%+ industry growth guidance, analyst avg target $578 vs current $603). LLY holds on the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program launching July 1, which drives volume growth over price cuts (stock surged +7.1% on June 26 on this news, analyst avg target $1,221). Key macro events: FOMC minutes July 8, weekly jobless claims July 9, CPI July 14. Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% under Warsh data-dependence framework. Sector rotation from tech to healthcare/financials creates near-term tech headwind, offset by AMAT and AMD's AI structural tailwinds. Blackout: LRCX (earnings July 29).
